title: graceful-shed-adapter-priority-curve-hotpatch
author: Asha Iyer
release_notes: Hotfix: add a latency-driven graceful-shed adapter and a prioritized fallback curve to reduce regional SLO breaches during KV-pressure spikes. Includes new telemetry and a guarded rollout path.
description: Context: Several customers experienced short-lived regional latency surges that pushed SLOs over thresholds when KV pressure spiked and autoscaling lagged. This PR adds a lightweight, in-runtime graceful-shed adapter that applies a priority curve to incoming requests and an atomic fallback proxy that routes non-critical traffic to a cheaper slow-path model or cached response. Motivation: reduce tail-latency SLO violations with minimal customer-visible errors and without requiring heavy infra changes. Summary of changes: 1) runtime/eviction/graceful_shed_adapter.go - new adapter implementing a priority curve (request priority, tenant weight, recent success rate) and decision function that returns {accept, deprioritize, route-to-fallback}. 2) runtime/fallback/proxy.go - atomic fallback proxy that preserves KV snapshot headers and attempts soft-prefetch before falling back. 3) telemetry/metrics.yaml - new metrics: shed.adapter.decisions, shed.adapter.latency_before_after, fallback.proxy.hit_rate. 4) scripts/rollout/gradual-enable.sh - orchestration helper to enable adapter across regions with staged weights. 5) unit and integration test additions under runtime/*_test.go and e2e/slowpath_simulator.go. Rollout plan: staged rollout by region using staged weights (10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%) with automatic rollback if region SLO regressions > 2 p.p. in 10m window. Feature gated behind env var ENABLE_GRACEFUL_SHED and a per-tenant opt-out. Checklist: [x] unit tests added [x] integration tests in CI [x] telemetry dashboards draft [x] safety gate scripts added [x] canary in us-west-2 run completed. Risk: decision function could be too aggressive and route valid traffic to slow-paths; mitigations include conservative initial curve, per-tenant opt-out, immediate rollback script, and a bounded retry policy in fallback. Merge: squash-merged after two approvals and green CI.

review_comments: Ravi Patel: Can we avoid per-request allocations in the decision hot-path? Suggest inlining a small object pool and reusing priority structs. Response from author: switched to object pool and added microbenchmarks showing 12% p90 improvement.

Lena Kim: We need clearer telemetry to detect aggressive shedding. Suggest metrics for per-tenant dropped_rate and time-to-restore. Response from author: added shed.adapter.tenant_dropped_rate and a README section for dashboards.

Ben Carlson: Is there a fallback storm risk if all regions route to slow-path at once? Response from author: added staggered regional rollout scripts and a circuit that enforces a global fallback cap; documented behavior in docs/ops/graceful_shed.md.
QA: e2e in canary showed 0.3% increase in immediate 503s but 22% reduction in 99.9th latency. Logged as acceptable tradeoff for canary.
test_plan: Unit+integration tests in CI; e2e canary in us-west-2 for 48h with staged weights (10/30/60/100); monitor shed.adapter.decisions, fallback.proxy.hit_rate, p50/p95/p99 latency and tenant_dropped_rate for regressions.
risk_and_mitigation: Primary risk: over-shedding causing customer visible errors. Mitigations: conservative default curve, per-tenant opt-out, immediate rollback script, bounded fallback concurrency, automated rollback if SLO regressions exceed threshold. Added feature flag and staged rollout scripts.
telemetry: New metrics: shed.adapter.decisions{region,result,priority_bucket}, shed.adapter.latency_before_after{region}, fallback.proxy.hit_rate, fallback.proxy.retries, shed.adapter.tenant_dropped_rate. Dashboards added under console/dashboards/shed_adapter.json and alerting rule to notify SRE on >2 p.p. SLO regression in 10m.
